perf-bot: ALERT: nightly-ci small-batch p95 +18% vs baseline for run 4294304321 — benchmark=small-batch/kvcache-serialize (seq_len=1024). Suspect commit: 6f2a3b4 (merge: 'kv: serialize prefetch change'). Details: https://ci.redwood.ai/runs/4294304321
perf-bot: attached artifacts: https://ci.redwood.ai/artifacts/4294304321/logs.tar.gz and flamegraph: https://ci.redwood.ai/artifacts/4294304321/flame.svg
Anna M: ack — on it, grabbing logs and pprof from the runner now
Raj P: thanks. can someone run `./tools/prof.sh --run 4294304321 --flame` and paste the flame? i'll pull node metrics (irq/softirq, context-switches)
Chris L: pinging infra: @infra-bot can we pin that runner image to stable until triage completes? :eyes:
infra-bot: Runner 7 pinned to image stable-2026-03-17 by Chris L
Anna M: quick scan: there's a large alloc spike in kvcache::serialize path around 00:12:40 — top allocs point to allocations of ~1MB buffers repeatedly
Anna M: reproducing locally with the failing commit shows p95 drops ~12% if I revert 6f2a3b4
Anna M: useful snippet from local repro:
```diff
- prefetch_buffers.reserve(n)
+ prefetch_buffers = Vec::with_capacity(n)
```
Raj P: hmm that change was intended to avoid copies earlier in the pipeline, but looks like it forces large contiguous allocations on the hot path
Chris L: can we try smallvec or a pooled allocator on that path? a bump allocator would avoid repeated mallocs
Anna M: opened a quick PR with smallvec fallback for <=64 bytes and arena for larger: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/pull/3214 — includes microbench
Raj P: nice. i'll queue a dedicated nightly run with PR applied and compare numbers. scheduling -> https://ci.redwood.ai/runs/4294304380
perf-bot: scheduled run 4294304380 for branch pr/3214
Chris L: if PR fixes, plan: canary merge and/or temporary rollback of merge 6f2a3b4 on Dedicated. ops and releases teams notified
Anna M: running the PR run now, grabbing pprof and memgraphs; will post results in ~20m
Raj P: looping in oncall @oncall in case we need emergency rollback for customer-facing traffic
oncall: oncall acknowledged
Anna M: RESULTS: run 4294304380 -> p95 -10% vs baseline, CPU p95 down ~6%, peak memory down ~120MB. flamegraph shows much smaller malloc path in serialize
Chris L: great. i'll request +1 and start canary rollout for the fix; ops to monitor
Raj P: adding note for postmortem and reminder to add regression test for kvcache allocation pattern
Anna M: thanks all :thumbsup:
